saints.name: St. Agnes
saints.title: Virgin and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A Roman girl of about thirteen who gave her life rather than her virginity, and whose name has been honored in the Church’s prayers ever since…
biography: Agnes was born about 291 of a noble Christian family of Rome. At twelve or thirteen she refused the son of the prefect Sempronius and the idols with him, professing Christ her only spouse; condemned in the persecution of Diocletian, she was dragged to a place of shame, where, her acts relate, her hair and an angel's garment covered her nakedness.

She died by the sword about 304 and was buried on the Via Nomentana, where Constantine's daughter Constantina raised over her grave the basilica that still stands. Ambrose and Prudentius sang her martyrdom, and her name was written in the Roman Canon, where it is read at every Mass.

Her name, in Greek meaning chaste and heard in Latin as agnus, a lamb, gave her feast its custom: two lambs are blessed each 21 January, and from their wool are woven the pallia the pope grants new archbishops. The maiden who chose death rather than yield her virginity is patroness of young girls, of chastity, and of the Children of Mary.
saints.knownFor: Virgin-martyr of the early Roman Church; her name in the Roman Canon.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 21 January
